correctness.rationale: The sorted tetrahedral vertex dot products and t in [0,1/2] force the two largest and two smallest vertex pairings, giving W=2(M+cm) for all directions including boundary ties by continuity. The ordered spherical chamber is one of 48 symmetric chambers, with dΩ=sinθ dθ dφ and θ<=atan(sec φ); five exact moments α,β,A,B,C match independent double quadrature to 3.2e-11. The rational derivative has numerator 2[-E+Dc], and independently coded rigorous Q-interval arithmetic bounds D in [0.0265181674,0.0265181678], E in [0.0161594304,0.0161594309], D-E in [0.0103587365,0.0103587374], proving unique c*=E/D in (0,1). 20,000 independent direct 12-vertex directional checks have max error 4.5e-16; t=0 mean-square width /8 exactly equals Finch unit-edge tetrahedral formula. The spherical ordered cone minimum occurs at its three extreme rays by positive linearity and Euclidean norm convexity, giving min W=2min(1,(1+c)/sqrt(3)); Cauchy–Schwarz gives max=2sqrt(1+c²). Finite checks corroborate rather than prove all directions.

Optimizing this natural intrinsic observable over the complete canonical tetrahedron-to-octahedron equal-truncation family yields an unexpected strict non-Archimedean interior minimizer, distinct from the separate transition in minimum-width direction. Its exact five-moment reduction and shape classification answer a natural non-tabular geometry question; neither elementary endpoint recomputation nor arbitrary parameter slicing.

The exact first and second width moments yield unique squared-CV optimizer t*=(1-(βA-αB)/(αC-βB))/2=0.195313965248...; directional minimum switches at (2-sqrt(3))/2. No broader truncations or shadow-area claims.
